notes:
The dates you gave, September 12 to 15, have already passed this year. I've assumed you mean September 2027. None of these venues has posted 2027 hours yet, so the hours below come from their own pages as they stand now. Check each one again closer to the trip. In 2027 those dates fall Sunday to Wednesday.

**1. Children's Museum of Manhattan (CMOM)**
- **Who it's for:** 
exhibits and programs for children ages 0-6
.
- **When:** 
Tuesday–Sunday, 10 am–5 pm
 on its current plan-your-visit page. Its visitor guidelines say 
July–September: Monday–Sunday
, which doesn't match the other pages. Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday look open either way. Monday, September 13, 2027 is uncertain.
- **Daily programs:** 
Circle Time runs 10:30–11:00 am
.
- **Price:** The pages I read don't give a current ticket price. They say 
you'll save $1 when you book online
.
- **Source:** Children's Museum of Manhattan, 212 West 83rd Street.

**2. Central Park Zoo**
- **Who it's for:** There is no preschool-specific program. A child 3 to 12 pays $16.95, and 
a child 2 and under is free
.
- **When:** Its posted hours for 
April 2 – October 31, 2026
 are 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM Monday to Friday and 10:00 AM to 5:30 PM on weekends. 
Last entry is 1 hour prior to closing.
 The posted hours stop at March 2027, so September 2027 hours aren't up yet.
- **Feedings:** The site's sample day lists 
a 10:40 AM penguin feeding and an 11:30 AM sea lion feeding
.
- **Price:** A general admission adult ticket is $22.95.
- **Source:** Central Park Zoo (Wildlife Conservation Society).

**3. Brooklyn Children's Museum**
- **Who it's for:** Its own page mentions 
the toddler-favorite Totally Tots
 exhibit, and I didn't find an age range on its site.
- **When:** 
Wednesday – Sunday, 10 am – 5 pm, closed Monday and Tuesday
. In September 2027 that means Sunday and Wednesday are open, and Monday and Tuesday are closed.
- **Price:** 
General admission is $15 per person.
 It's 
free every Thursday from 2 pm–5 pm
, which falls outside your dates.
- **Source:** Brooklyn Children's Museum.

I didn't find a playground or an aquarium page I could stand behind. I ran out of searches before reading the New York Aquarium's own page, so I'm not recommending it.
